description: Deterministic dataset parameters shared byte-for-byte between the Java and Rust suites. Every checksum function is a pure function of its size/count parameters, independent of which CPU or NUMA node the thread computing it actually ran on — placement can only change how fast these run (the mechanism this lab measures via the native-Linux evidence run), never whether the checksum is correct. Real topology facts (isolated core id, SMT sibling, same/remote NUMA node) are probed at runtime from /sys on Linux and are never hardcoded, per the 'hardcoding CPU ids' trap this lab documents.
correctnessInvariant: For every dataset, the checksum is identical across every placement target that could actually be resolved on the current host, and identical to the unpinned baseline's checksum, in both languages.
